speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a chronic cough and have experienced recurrent bouts of bronchitis; to narrow this down, how long has your cough been persistent?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The description of a chronic cough with copious, thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for 11 years, worsened in the morning, is classic for bronchiectasis rather than simple recurrent bronchitis. Given your age and non-smoker status, we need to confirm the airway dilation. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CTA.
